name: Docusign, Inc.
sector: Application Software — e-signature / Intelligent Agreement Management
moat_justification: Category leader in e-signature (1.9M+ customers, 180+ countries) with enterprise workflow embedding and an IAM platform ramping to 15.1% of ARR, but the core signature product is commoditizing (Adobe, Dropbox, PandaDoc, platform bundling), growth has decelerated to high single digits, and the ROIC proxy history is too distorted by a near-zero invested-capital base to evidence a wide moat — recent proxy readings (FY24 7.5%, FY25 11.7%, FY26 20.2%) are improving off buyback-shrunk equity rather than proven through a cycle. GAAP gross margin is stable at ~79% (FY24 79.3%, FY25 79.1%, FY26 79.4%).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SHARES_FALLBACK: no diluted share count filed for 2018, 2019 — those history years use the basic / outstanding / dei count recorded in the shares_tag column; per-share history there is approximate

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 2.09 vs 3-yr median 1.47 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.1%) vs bull-case tier C (11.1%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Durable cash compounder with a narrow moat (5/10) — even on the current TTM base of $3.04/sh, weighted IRR is only 9.2% at $74.65 and no scenario clears 15%; it clears the 15% hurdle only under ~$37.65.
moat_for: E-signature category leader: 1.9M+ customers across 180+ countries, default brand for the workflow
Enterprise workflow embedding and integrations create real switching friction in regulated, high-volume signing
IAM platform expanding the surface: 2.3% of ARR (Jan 2025) to 15.1% (Jul 2026), guided 18-19% exiting FY27
Stable ~79% GAAP gross margin and ~31% non-GAAP operating margin; no debt, heavy buybacks
moat_against: Core e-signature is commoditizing: Adobe Sign, Dropbox Sign, PandaDoc and platform bundles compete on price
Revenue growth decelerated from 17% 5-yr CAGR to ~8-9% — the category is maturing
SMB/self-serve segment has weak switching costs; retention has hovered near 100% rather than expanding
IAM/AI agreement tooling is contested by every suite vendor; the agreement-data advantage is not yet proven durable
